claim: In an Eisenberg–Noe star clearing network with \(m\ge1\) targets, unit outside assets, equal initial net worth \(x\in(0,1/(m+1))\) for every bank, and a source whose liabilities are entirely interbank and split equally among the targets, let independent primary loss shocks share survival function \(S\) and be capped at the unit outside-asset value. If \(S(0)=1\) and \(\log S\) is convex on \([0,(m+1)x]\), then the probability that a shock to the source alone defaults all targets is \(S((m+1)x)\ge S(x)^{m+1}\), the probability that all banks default through independent direct shocks. The inequality is strict when \(\log S\) is strictly convex on the relevant interval; in particular, every non-degenerate mixture of exponential rates gives strict inequality at every feasible threshold, while a pure exponential law gives equality.

correctness.rationale: The star liability construction makes the cascade event exactly \(\{X_0>(m+1)x\}\); the cap is inactive at this threshold. Independent direct defaults have probability \(S(x)^{m+1}\). Convexity of \(\log S\) and \(\log S(0)=0\) yield \(S((m+1)x)\ge S(x)^{m+1}\), strictly for strict convexity. The two-rate witness has exact gap \(\tfrac14(e^{-1/5}-e^{-2})^2>0\).

No empirical calibration is claimed; real bank shock distributions may be dependent and may not have log-convex survival.

value.rationale: The exact all-feasible-threshold result identifies a sharp boundary between homogeneous exponential shocks (equality) and non-degenerate exponential-rate mixtures (strict strong contagion), extending the published IFR and asymptotic Pareto-tail comparisons to a light-tailed heterogeneous-shock class. It clarifies a model-relevant probability comparison without claiming empirical or aggregate-loss conclusions.
